entities.name: Query PPi-PFK
observations: 341 aa protein; predicted molecular weight 36.1 kDa and theoretical pI 5.50.
Contains Pfam PFK domain PF00365 spanning residues 2–296.
Strong full-length homology to reviewed bacterial pyrophosphate–fructose 6-phosphate 1-phosphotransferases: 73.3% identity to UniProt Q59126, 72.1% to Q9AGC0, and 68.4% to O08333.

Likely catalyzes reversible phosphorylation of D-fructose 6-phosphate using inorganic pyrophosphate, producing fructose 1,6-bisphosphate and phosphate; exact substrate specificity is inferred from homology.
Likely requires Mg2+ and functions in cytoplasmic carbohydrate metabolism, especially glycolysis and potentially gluconeogenesis.
Reference proteins are annotated as homodimeric or homotetrameric and non-allosteric; oligomeric state of the query is inferred, not experimentally established.

entities.name: Q59126
observations: Reviewed UniProt reference: pyrophosphate–fructose 6-phosphate 1-phosphotransferase from Amycolatopsis methanolica; 73.3% identity and 100% coverage to the query.
Annotated EC 2.7.1.90, Mg2+ cofactor, cytoplasmic localization, and glycolysis/carbohydrate degradation role.

entities.name: PPi-dependent F6P phosphorylation
observations: beta-D-fructose 6-phosphate + diphosphate = beta-D-fructose 1,6-bisphosphate + phosphate + H(+). Rhea RHEA:13613; direction is reversible/undetermined in the annotation.

entities.name: Mg2+
observations: Magnesium ion is annotated as the cofactor for close reviewed PPi-dependent phosphofructokinase homologs.

entities.name: Glycolysis
observations: The homologous enzyme participates at the fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate step of glycolysis and can support gluconeogenic flux because the PPi-driven reaction is reversible.

entities.name: Cytoplasm
observations: Close reviewed homologs are annotated as cytoplasmic enzymes; the query is predicted to be cytoplasmic by homology.
